title: [Keyboard Manager] glitches (requires restart) under heavy load
author: DavidBabel
summary: The report is strong enough for a maintainer-side Keyboard Manager stress repro, and its “stuck Win key until key press + disable/re-enable” behavior points to the same modifier-state class as the newer swapped-modifier bug rather than a vague performance complaint.

judgment.rationale: Even though the report says the trigger is random under load, it specifies the exact remap (Alt -> Win), the visible stuck-key effect, and the manual reset path, which is enough to investigate the modifier state machine.
evidence: The report uses a single remap: Alt is remapped to the Windows key.
Under heavy CPU spikes, the real Windows-key behavior becomes latched until Keyboard Manager is disabled and the Windows key is pressed once.
The reporter adds that trying to revert to a previous version can also break the settings flow, which suggests state persistence or cleanup concerns rather than a one-off application conflict.
No assignee, linked PR, or open duplicate was found in the current issue thread.
judgment.recommended_action: Run a local stress repro focused on modifier state cleanup for remapped Alt/Win paths and design a fix that cannot strand the effective Win key down after delayed or interrupted input sequences.

fix_assessment.rationale: This still looks like a PowerToys keyboard-state bug rather than an external hardware issue, and there is no linked fix attempt yet.

proposed_fixes.title: Harden remapped modifier release and recovery under delayed input conditions
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The best current hypothesis is that heavy load exposes a path where the remapped Alt->Win state is injected or suppressed asymmetrically, leaving the effective Win key logically down until another explicit key transition forces the state machine to recover.
plan: Reproduce the Alt->Win remap under input or CPU stress and capture the exact sequence that strands the Win state.
Normalize key-up handling and recovery for remapped modifier keys even when the injected/suppressed event pair is delayed or interrupted.
Add an engine regression that proves a remapped modifier cannot stay latched after the physical keys are released.
verification: Under the failing remap and a stress condition, confirm Win+R or similar behavior no longer appears spontaneously after the physical keys are released.
Disable/re-enable and settings-save flows should continue to work after the fix.

confidence.rationale: The stuck-Win symptom clearly points to modifier-state handling, but the exact stressed sequence still needs a direct repro to isolate the failing release path.

issue_context.summary: A remapped Alt key can leave the effective Windows key stuck under heavy load until Keyboard Manager is disabled and the Windows key is pressed manually.
known_information: The issue is on Windows 11 and PowerToys 0.101.2262.
The reporter uses Alt -> Win because the physical Alt key is broken.
The stuck state persists until manual recovery rather than clearing on its own.
No maintainer response or linked work is present.
inferences: The failure likely sits in the Keyboard Manager engine’s modifier state tracking, because the user can clear it only with a real key transition.
The heavy-load qualifier suggests timing-sensitive cleanup rather than a static mapping configuration error.
issue_context.analysis: This should not be turned into a reporter information request yet. The remaining work is maintainer-side stress reproduction and engine tracing, which maps better to a reproduce action plus a tentative design hypothesis.
initial_investigation: The current open-keyboard issue set does not expose another exact duplicate, but the symptom class overlaps with #50007’s stuck-modifier report.
Current Keyboard Manager tests already include stuck-key hardening for some paths, which makes a targeted engine regression the right next validation surface.

actions.label: Approve Keyboard Manager stress-state design
actions.note: The hypothesis is useful now, but the exact delayed-release branch should be captured in a failing repro or engine test before code lands.

actions.label: Reproduce stuck Win after Alt remap under load
actions.note: Exercise the exact Alt -> Win mapping while generating CPU or UI load to trap the latching sequence.

prerequisites: Use a target app where unexpected Win-key behavior is obvious, such as Win+R opening Run.
steps: Enable the Alt -> Win remap and begin interacting with the machine under moderate to heavy CPU load.
Trigger ordinary Alt-key usage patterns and then release the physical keys.
Watch for later keypresses such as R acting as if Win is still held.
Press the real Windows key once and compare whether that clears the latched state.
reproduce.expected_result: The remapped modifier should never remain logically held once the physical key is released, even under load.
